(1) INTERVAL BYPASS: robots_allowed fetches robots.txt with requests.get DIRECTLY (src/sources/base.py:157), outside _respect_rate_limit, and polite_get calls it BEFORE _respect_rate_limit(domain) (:249 then :255). On the first fetch to any domain in a process _last_request_at has no entry, so wait is 0 and the page request follows the robots request immediately — TWO REQUESTS TO THE SAME HOST BACK TO BACK WITH NO ENFORCED INTERVAL, on every domain, every run. The 2026-08-09 batch did it four times (example.com, investmentpolicy.unctad.org, uncitral.un.org, digitallibrary.un.org — the control row is a domain like any other). METHODOLOGY Part III publishes 'I do not send automated queries to any single domain at intervals shorter than three seconds.' Fix is about two lines and is NOT applied: src/ is unapproved. (2) WILDCARD NON-SUPPORT: Python's RobotFileParser implements NO * or $ path wildcards — RuleLine.applies_to is `self.path == "*" or filename.startswith(self.path)` — so this project's robots layer SILENTLY IGNORES EVERY Disallow rule using a wildcard, on every host, and always has, while METHODOLOGY Part III publishes 'I follow standard robot exclusion protocols.' Found by the integrity officer restoring the missing colon to digitallibrary.un.org's malformed 'Disallow /record/*/export/*$' line and finding can_fetch still returned True. (3) NOT A DEFECT, A POLICY QUESTION FOR THE OPERATOR: digitallibrary.un.org publishes 'Crawl-Delay: 5'; MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS is 3.0 and grep for crawl_delay across *.py returns nothing, so the value is exposed by the parser and read by no code path. Crawl-Delay is a non-standard extension absent from RFC 9309, so this is a gap against a host's expressed preference rather than against the exclusion standard. The 2026-08-01 record already drafted the wording — 'or shorter than a longer minimum where the source publishes one' — for GDELT, a source never adopted.
